entityDescription:
The Space Exploration Institute, SPACE-X for short, is a non-profit research institute located in Neuchâtel, Switzerland. Expertise of the staff covers several fields of science and engineering, including planetary science, astronomy, geology and system engineering for space science instrument development.

Space Exploration Institute Goals:
To Develop the Space Exploration Activity, in particular to develop the research link to the planetary exploration by:
- Perform research on the Moon, Mars, planetary bodies of the solar system included studies on the ices deposits and past or present life traces (Exo/Astrobiology)
- Contribution/Elaboration of science proposals in order to participate to the future missions which explore the solar system
- Develop the Science Instruments link to this research
- Operate the on-board instruments, process, analyse the science data output
- Promote science to the public, at schools , colleges, universities over Neuchatel, Switzerland and around the Earth.

entityDescription: Square Peg Communications Inc. Square Peg produces wideband Radio Link Simulators / Satellite Link Emulators, and Physical Layer Testers for Inmarsat networks, including Inmarsat-Aero, Inmarsat-C, Swift 64, Fleet Broadband, Swift Broadband, BGAN and IsatData Pro. Square Peg also develops and supports operational hub station equipment, and provides DSP-based modems and other OEM products for integration into its customers' own products. entityDescription:
The Shadow Robot Company is an independent robotics research Entity, developing humanoid robot technologies. The company was founded in 1997 from a group of independent robotics researchers. At present, the company specialises in the development of advanced robotics products and components, most notable the Air Muscle and Dextrous Hand technologies.
Shadow's leading product is the Dextrous Hand, which Shadow has worked on since 1998, funded successively by a SMART award, NESTA and by sales to customers. The Shadow Dextrous Hand is the most advanced robotic hand available in the world, offering the full movement capability of the human hand. Customers include NASA and Carnegie-Mellon University. The hand, first completed in 2000, was at the time the most dexterous robot hand in the world. Shadow is currently working on the commercialisation of this system, which requires development of supporting infrastructure as well as bringing to production advanced robotic systems.

entityDescription:
STAM is a private engineering SME headquartered in Genoa, Italy, specializing in delivering advanced engineering services to industries worldwide. Initially supported by seed funding from the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Technology Transfer Programme to develop an innovative gearbox system, STAM has since expanded its expertise across multiple sectors, including defense, robotics, security and transport, energy, and environmental technologies. The company boasts a highly qualified workforce, with 90% holding at least a master’s degree and over 70% possessing an MSc in Engineering.
STAM has been a trusted collaborator of ESA since 1999, actively contributing to initiatives such as the Innovation Triangle Initiative and the Technology Transfer Programmes. Notable projects include its role as the main subcontractor in the ADRiNET project, which focused on developing a parametric simulator for active debris removal (ADR) using nets. This effort culminated in a successful parabolic flight campaign in Ottawa, Canada, validating the ADR concept. The technology was further enhanced through the EU’s H2020 ADR1EN Project, encompassing upscaling activities, thermal-vacuum testing at Thales Alenia Space Italy, full-scale ground experiments, and the creation of a comprehensive business plan for ADR systems.
STAM has also led ESA projects like “Hermetic Sealing for Rotating Shaft,” where it developed and tested innovative mechanical sealing solutions. More recently, STAM was named ESA’s National Technology Broker for Italy, tasked with driving technology transfer initiatives. This role involves technology scouting, promotional campaigns, and developing business models for high-potential use cases, helping research centers unlock the value of their intellectual property and facilitating spin-in and spin-off technology transfers between terrestrial and space applications. Through this role, STAM also manages ESA’s Spark Funding in collaboration with the Italian Space Agency (ASI).
As part of its contributions to ESA’s Space Rider program, STAM developed a business model emphasizing microgravity research in advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnologies. The model bridges the current cost gap for space missions by leveraging intellectual property to attract private and institutional investors, fostering a venture-builder approach to innovation.
Thanks to its extensive portfolio of R&D projects, STAM has forged strong partnerships with hundreds of international companies and research institutions, including leading organizations and key stakeholders in the space sector.

entityDescription: Leiden University is the oldest university in the Netherlands. It was founded in February 1575, as a gift from William of Orange to the citizens of Leiden who had withstood a long siege by the Spaniards. In Leiden there are approximately 17,000 students and 4,000 staff members. The University consists of 6 faculties, a School of Education (teacher training), and a Campus in The Hague. The University houses the faculties of Archaeology, Humanities, Law, Medicine/LUMC (Leiden University Medical Center), Mathematics and Natural Sciences and Social and Behavioural Sciences.The faculties offer a varied range of bachelor's, master's and PhD programmes. In addition, three other units offer post-academic training: the Institute for Environmental Sciences (CML), the School of Education (ICLON) and Campus The Hague. The latter specialises in post-academic training in the field of law and political science for those working in the public sector, the legal sector or the corporate world.

entityDescription: The Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute (Swiss TPH) is Switzerland’s leading public and global health institution. Associated with the University of Basel, Swiss TPH combines research, service provision and education and training at the local, national and international level. Over 700 employees and students from more than 70 nations work at Swiss TPH in the fields of infectious and non-communicable diseases, society and health, environment and health as well as health systems and interventions. Founded in 1943, Swiss TPH is a public non-commercial organization partially supported by the Swiss Federal Government and the Cantons of Basel and Basel Country. However, over 65 % of Swiss TPH’s funds are competitively acquired through bidding for projects and research grants. The institute’s mandate is to contribute to the improvement of population health internationally and nationally through excellence in research, services, teaching and training.

entityDescription:
Terma provides mission-critical solutions for the aerospace, defense, and security industries, guided by one overarching purpose: Securing People through Advanced Technology. Our strength lies not only in engineering and manufacturing, but in our ability to apply these capabilities in complex operational environments, tailored to the specific needs of our customers. We are recognized for our expertise in mission-critical software, systems integration, and secure data transfer across domains. BUSINESS AREAS: Space designs and delivers electronics, software, and support services for satellites, control centre's, and testing systems. With strong heritage in European institutional programs, the Business Area is expanding into global New Space markets with increasing focus on defense. Terma continues to develop and deliver advanced Star Trackers and other critical satellite technologies, serving customers across Europe, the U.S., Asia Pacific, and the Middle East. Surveillance & Mission Systems delivers advanced radar and command-and-control (C2)technologies for single-domain operations – such as air defense and naval missions – as well as multi-domain scenarios involving intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance. The SCANTER radar family remains a core offering, particularly in coastal surveillance and port and airport traffic control. Radar applications for naval vessels continue to grow, including a milestone contract in 2024/25 with the Canadian Coast Guard for anew class of multi-purpose vessels. Terma also advanced its drone detection and classification capabilities using artificial intelligence, attracting strong interest from customers worldwide. The Business Area secured a key order from the Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organization for the BMD-Flex C2system and was appointed system integrator for Denmark’s new Very Short-Range Air Defense (VSHORAD) system. The growing demand for Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) further strengthens this Business Area’s strategic position. As the protection of vital infrastructure becomes an increasingly urgent priority for governments and private operators alike, Terma’s integrated radar and software solutions are uniquely suited to securing critical assets against evolving threats, from conventional intrusions to emerging challenges. This positions Surveillance& Mission Systems as a key enabler in the safeguarding of essential societal Infrastructure across land, sea, under water and air.
Self-Protection Systems provides integrated electronic warfare solutions for military aircraft, enhancing survivability through systems such as the ALQ-213 controller and Advanced Threat Displays. The Business Area also delivers Terma’s operationally proven 3D-Audio solution, improving aircrew situational awareness and reducing fatigue. In 2024/25, demand was at a record high, with continued traction across fighters, helicopters, mobility aircraft, and collaborative combat systems. Support & Services ensures high availability and lifecycle support for Terma solutions across civil and defense applications. With scalable maintenance offerings and the Terma Lifecare service portfolio, the Business Area provides everything from unit-level service to countrywide solutions. In 2024/25, Support & Services expanded its presence in the Middle East and Asia, introduced cyber-hardened radar solutions, and launched a new cybersecurity subscription model. The Business Area also initiated OEM support activities to meet growing regional demand and support defense procurement across Denmark and the Nordics.

The growing demand for Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) further strengthens this Business Area’s strategic position. As the protection of vital infrastructure becomes an increasingly urgent priority for governments and private operators alike, Terma’s integrated radar and software solutions are uniquely suited to securing critical assets against evolving threats, from conventional intrusions to emerging challenges. This positions Surveillance& Mission Systems as a key enabler in the safeguarding of essential societal Infrastructure across land, sea, under water and air.
Self-Protection Systems provides integrated electronic warfare solutions for military aircraft, enhancing survivability through systems such as the ALQ-213 controller and Advanced Threat Displays. The Business Area also delivers Terma’s operationally proven 3D-Audio solution, improving aircrew situational awareness and reducing fatigue. In 2024/25, demand was at a record high, with continued traction across fighters, helicopters, mobility aircraft, and collaborative combat systems. Support & Services ensures high availability and lifecycle support for Terma solutions across civil and defense applications. With scalable maintenance offerings and the Terma Lifecare service portfolio, the Business Area provides everything from unit-level service to countrywide solutions. In 2024/25, Support & Services expanded its presence in the Middle East and Asia, introduced cyber-hardened radar solutions, and launched a new cybersecurity subscription model. The Business Area also initiated OEM support activities to meet growing regional demand and support defense procurement across Denmark and the Nordics.

entityDescription:
TeSA Lab (www.tesa.prd.fr ) is a private non-profit organisation, aiming at performing Research studies and PhD in Telecommunications for Space and Aeronautics, and in related domains.
This non-profit organisation acts as a Research Lab, with a Scientific Committee, wellcoming research engineers, academics from partner members, together with around 20 PhD students and post-docs. This collaborative Research Laboratory includes academic members from French universities (engineer schools) ENAC, ISAE-Supaero, INPT and IMT Atlantique, as well as industrial partners (Thales Alenia Space and Rockwell Collins France) and institutional partners as the French Space Agency (CNES), the Institute of Technology (IRT) Saint Exupery and the Air Navigation Services (DSNA).
TeSA is a structure unique in France, around which revolve various industrial, institutional and academic organizations. This has allowed it to develop for more than 10 years a practice in collaboration for applied research, with high efficiency and, whenever necessary, a guarantee of confidentiality.
The expertise of TeSA covers: 
•	digital communications: synchronisation, equalization, waveform modulation, source and channel coding, spectrum surveillance, MIMO systems,…
•	networks : transmission techniques, architectures, routing, multiple access, security,… 
•	signal and image processing : navigation and positioning, radar signal processing, estimation, detection and classification, fusion,…
in application domains such as 
•	space and aeronautical communication systems, 
•	Earth observation, 
•	localization and navigation.

entityDescription:
Instituto Superior Técnico aims to contribute to the development of society, promoting and sharing excellence in higher education in the fields of Architecture, Engineering, Science and Technology. Técnico offers Bachelor, Master and PhD programmes, lifelong training and develops Research, Development and Innovation (RD&I) activities, which are essential to provide an education based on the top international standards.

The 1st centenary of Técnico, in 2011, marked a historic milestone in a School that keeps its traditions and values, projecting them into a global and highly skilled world. Innovation, Knowledge and Technology are Técnico’s guiding principles, which promote excellence and fit the requirements of a knowledge-based society.

Técnico is part of Universidade de Lisboa, the largest and the most competitive university in Portugal, and is recognised as a prestigious school at national and international level, namely in the fields of Architecture, Engineering, Science and Technology. It comprises Portugal’s most prestigious Laboratories and RD&I centres.

Técnico offers a wide variety of courses to study, both at the undergraduate and graduate level and it is actively involved in several international mobility programmes. IST has significantly contributed to create cutting-edge science and technology, which is the main goal of the school.
